newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt trades at higher levels, but in range.
newsitem.headline: German debt trades at higher levels, but in range.

text.p: German debt remained at higher levels in late trading on Wednesday with dealers forecasting range-trade for the next sessions as the market eyes year-end holiday celebrations and feels ever less inclined to trade.

By 1532 GMT the March Bund futures contract traded up 23 basis points at 100.04, close to the top of the day's range between 100.18 and 99.89. The April 2006 cash bond traded at 102.59 compared with its closing price os 102.38 on Tuesday.
The market was buoyed by the recovery in U.S. Treasuries late on Tuesday after the Fed kept interest rates steady and on Wednesday two additional factors supported prices.
Softer than expected November German M3 money supply growth as well as slightly stronger Treasuries both helped the market.

M3 measured eight percent after 8.4 percent in October and raised some hopes that the Bundesbank could be prompted to nudge its main money market rate, the repo, lower at its final policy-setting session of the year on Thursday.
But the majority of independent economists expect the central bank to leave all rates steady, reserving any room to nudge rates lower until next year.
Bond market dealers expect a similar course of action.
"There is really no need to do anything at the moment," said one trader.

As many players have closed their books for the year and are more eager to turn their attention to holiday parties than trading, dealers predicted range trading between 100.20 and 99.70 for the next several sessions.
The Bundesbank will hold a news conference after its meeting on Thursday to explain its new money supply target to the public.
